name.text: Calculating the length in a triangle given two sines and an angle

questiontext.text:
Two sides of a triangle have lengths \(a={@a@}\) and \(b={@b@}\). The included angle is \(C={@C_deg@}^\circ\).

Use the cosine rule \(c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C\) to calculate the length of side \(c\).

Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

[[input:ans1]][[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

To calculate the length of side \(c\), we use the cosine rule:

\(c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab\cos C\)

Step 1: Identify the given values.

The two known sides are \(a={@a@}\) and \(b={@b@}\), and the included angle is \(C={@C_deg@}^\circ\).

Step 2: Substitute into the cosine rule.

\( c^2=({@a@})^2+({@b@})^2-2({@a@})({@b@})\cos({@C_deg@}^\circ)\)

Step 3: Evaluate the expression.

Calculate the squares of the side lengths and evaluate the cosine of the included angle. Then simplify:

\(c^2={@c_sq@}\)

Step 4: Find the length of side \(c\).

Take the positive square root because a side length must be positive:

\(c=\sqrt{{@c_sq@}}\)

Therefore, the length of side \(c\), to 2 decimal places, is {@round(c_ans*100)/100@}.
